cards.b: Electrons move from the cloth to the rod: rod negative, cloth positive. Only negative charge moves.

short.q: Explain why a polythene rod becomes negatively charged when rubbed with a cloth.
short.model: Electrons are transferred from the cloth to the rod by friction. The rod gains extra negative charge, and the cloth is left positive.
points: rod has an excess of negative charge

short.q: A current of 0.50 A flows for 2.0 minutes. Calculate the charge that flows.
Describe an experiment to find the resistance of a resistor.
short.model: Connect the resistor in series with an ammeter and variable resistor with a supply; connect a voltmeter across the resistor. Record V and I for several settings and calculate R = V ÷ I for each, then average.
points: ammeter in series, voltmeter in parallel
several readings of V and I

short.q: A wire has resistance 8.0 Ω. Predict the resistance of a wire of the same material and length but double the diameter. Explain.
short.model: Doubling the diameter makes the area four times larger, so resistance is 8.0 ÷ 4 = 2.0 Ω (R is inversely proportional to area).

short.q: State the difference between e.m.f. and p.d.
short.model: E.m.f. is the work done by a source per unit charge around the whole circuit; p.d. is the work done per unit charge passing between two points (across a component).
points: p.d.: between two points / across component
